details:
REVISIONS WILL BE MADE I RECEIVE NEW INFORMATION ON THIS SUBJECT!

This is request is going to get a bit technical so please bare this in mind as this is something that not only would improve performance for some users, but ensure that as more headsets are made that they will also be compatible with some shader elements, especially those involving screen shaders for worlds and avatars, especially horror maps.

So, why the disclaimer? For a long time, or basically since 2018, some companies in the VR space began to release hardware that offered a wider field of view which for some helps out with immersion. Pimax is famous for the generous about of Horizontal FOV they offer their users, but here lies the major issue especially with regards to how they were able to achieve this wide FOV effect. As explained by an Nvidia representative at Siggraph 2018, in order for VR headsets to a wider field of view the displays cannot be parallel/coplanar, they would have to angled or canted in order to accomodate for better immersion[1].

As of today there are various devices out in the market that use these types of display technologies, one of them being Pimax, but some of the most popular headsets out on the market, such as but not limited to the Valve Index and HP Reverb G2, use non-parallel displays. The major problem is self explanatory: these headsets calculate things such as the view and projection matrices differently from each eye (further data on each headset can be shown here [2]), and Unity's native VR projection only supports coplanar displays, which means when using canted displays there could be a chance that some shaders can lead to even more potential discomfort and eye strain if this is not corrected properly[3]. But from looking into this subject further, VRChat has partial support for canted displays [4], in that according to the Pimax game compatibiliy chart it is recommended that users play with Parallel Projection On to avoid discomfort when in VR (check the "official list for pimax" tab in [4]). 

What is Parallel Projection? To best summarize what parallel projection, it is a rendering technique that ensures that the view and projection matrices are parallel while mantaining their wider field of view to support titles that assume VR displays were going to be parallel[5]. Pimax is normally the example but Valve uses parallel projection in order to support older titles and would want to urge developers to begin to support for non-parallel rendering[6]. Not only should users not have to do this, but it's more expensive to render as the headset is processing more pixel data, which for a Pimax headset is a 30% increase on GPU Usage[7]. Not only that, but some headsets with canted displays do not natively support parallel projection, the Reverb G2 does not even support this rendering technique.

With all of the things I mentioned what could be done to remedy this issue? I know VRChat does not like to use other Unity scripts, but this would have to be done on the developer end, to have a script on the VRC Player Cam to convert the headset's native frustum to properly render both shaders that rely on the unity camera data to convert verts to screen data (like a billboard shader) as well as fixing particle billboarding for the projection and view matrices. An example of a fix can be found in [8].

Instead of putting the burden of fixing this issue on those who make custom shaders (who also can't use custom scripts to address this issue), it should be the VRChat developement team to either provide new shader properties for us to experiment with for custom vertex shaders or VRChat reworks the VRViewer so that past shaders can have better compatibility with asymmetrical frustums.

[1] https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/turing-multi-view-rendering-vrworks/

[2] https://risa2000.github.io/hmdgdb/

[3] https://iliaskapouranis.com/2020/08/13/single-pass-stereo-wrong-depth-cues-discomfort-and-potential-risks/

[4] https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11ljKyF0eMgY3qqZWjVVBvI0brfv9IxocXjroYtJyTlY/edit#gid=2033767133

[5] https://risa2000.github.io/vrdocs/docs/hmd_fov_calculation#parallel-projection

[6] https://www.valvesoftware.com/en/index/deep-dive/fov

[7] https://community.openmr.com/t/closer-look-at-pimax-parallel-projection/20510

[8] https://github.com/koochyrat/SteamVRFrustumAdjust
title: VRChat needs to start taking better account of headsets with canted display technologies to improve shader compatibility, performance, and comfort for these users.
